novel.justification: At least four compatible assignments is the first nondegenerate resolution at which a paired rectangle can contain more than one complementary assignment pair.

Large marketplace experiments can allocate at least four units per required randomization-support point on the buyer side; the condition is a transparent finite threshold, not an asymptotic approximation.
The same finite threshold is implementable on the seller side even when the two population sizes are unequal.

standard.name: Independent two-sided complete randomization at fixed treated counts

assumptions.condition: \(Y\) is fixed with respect to the random draw \(Z\).
For every \((i,j)\in B\times S\), \(Y_{ij}\) depends on an assignment only through \((z_i^B,z_j^S)\) at the fixed margins.

standard.name: Local two-sided exposure restriction at fixed margins

novel.justification: A prespecified randomization-support floor is operationally meaningful because it fixes the attainable granularity of an exact test before outcomes are observed.

standard.name: Additive sharp constant-effect null, two-sided total-effect variant

definitions.name: Common half-sum support
definitions.construction: \(H(a,b)=\{z\in\{0,1\}^{L}:\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}a_\ell z_\ell=n_B,\ \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}b_\ell z_\ell=n_S\}\).

definitions.name: Rectangular retention
definitions.construction: \(F(a,b)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}a_\ell b_\ell\).

definitions.name: Admissible covering rectangular profiles
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_{n_B,n_S}(R)=\{\rho=(L,a,b):L\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ a_\ell,b_\ell\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\ (\ell\in[L]),\ \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}a_\ell=2n_B,\ \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}b_\ell=2n_S,\ h(a,b)\ge R\}\).

definitions.name: Optimal retention frontier
definitions.construction: \(\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)=\max\{F(a,b):(L,a,b)\in\mathcal A_{n_B,n_S}(R)\}\), with value \(-\infty\) when the class is empty.

definitions.name: Finite residual catalog
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_R=\{c=(m,u,v,p,q):1\le m\le2R,\ u,v\in\mathbb Z_{>0}^{m},\ A=\sum_i u_i\le2R,\ D=\sum_i v_i\le2R,\ 0\le p\le A,\ 0\le q\le D,\ 2N_c\ge R\}\), where \(N_c=\#\{J\subseteq[m]:\sum_{i\in J}u_i=p,\ \sum_{i\in J}v_i=q\}\).

definitions.name: Diagonal unit-residual subcatalog
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U_R=\{c=(m,u,v,p,q)\in\mathcal C_R:u_i=v_i=1\ \text{for every }i\in[m]\}\).

definitions.name: Catalog-induced profile
definitions.construction: For \(c=(m,u,v,p,q)\in\mathcal C_R\), set \(a_c=(n_B-p,n_B-A+p,u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) and \(b_c=(n_S-q,n_S-D+q,v_1,\ldots,v_m)\).

definitions.name: Affine phase score
definitions.construction: \(K_c=pq+(A-p)(D-q)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_iv_i\) and \(f_c(n_B,n_S)=2n_Bn_S-Dn_B-An_S+K_c\).

definitions.name: Published equal-square block comparator
definitions.construction: For \(n_B=n_S=n\), \(\Phi_n^{\mathrm{eq}}(R)=\max\{2nk:k\mid n,\ \binom{2n/k}{n/k}\ge R\}\), with value \(-\infty\) if the displayed set is empty; this is the best retention within the equal \(k\)-block family of Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis.

definitions.name: Covering paired partition and focal set
definitions.construction: Given \((L,a,b)\), choose ordered partitions \(\mathscr B=(B_1,\ldots,B_L)\) of \(B\) and \(\mathscr S=(S_1,\ldots,S_L)\) of \(S\) with \(|B_\ell|=a_\ell\) and \(|S_\ell|=b_\ell\); set \(P=(\mathscr B,\mathscr S)\) and \(U_P=\bigcup_{\ell=1}^{L}(B_\ell\times S_\ell)\).

definitions.name: Assignment incidence
definitions.construction: \(\nu(a,b)=h(a,b)(n_B!)^2(n_S!)^2\big/(\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}a_\ell!\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}b_\ell!)\).

definitions.name: Common-pattern then partition sampler
definitions.construction: Given the realized \(Z\), \(\mathsf{Sample}_{ZP}\) first draws \(z\) uniformly from \(H(a,b)\); independently on each market side it uniformly permutes treated labels into the indexed blocks with \(z_\ell=1\) and control labels into the indexed blocks with \(z_\ell=0\), cuts at the prescribed sizes, and reports only the resulting paired partition \(P\).

definitions.name: Observed outcome and joint-exposure arrays
definitions.construction: \(Y_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{ij}(z_i^B,z_j^S)\) for \((i,j)\in B\times S\), and \(X_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}}=z_\ell^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for \((i,j)\in B_\ell\times S_\ell\).

definitions.name: Null-adjusted focal outcomes
definitions.construction: For \((i,j)\in U_P\), \(Q_{\tau,ij}=Y_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\tau X_{ij}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

definitions.name: Focal-dyad difference in means
definitions.construction: For \(z\in H(a,b)\) and \(q_0\in\mathbb R^{U_P}\), \(D_z(q_0)=\frac{\sum_{\ell:z_\ell=1}\sum_{(i,j)\in B_\ell\times S_\ell}q_{0,ij}}{\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}a_\ell b_\ell z_\ell}-\frac{\sum_{\ell:z_\ell=0}\sum_{(i,j)\in B_\ell\times S_\ell}q_{0,ij}}{\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}a_\ell b_\ell(1-z_\ell)}\).

definitions.name: Exhaustive upper-tail randomization \(p\)-value
definitions.construction: \(p_\tau=h(a,b)^{-1}\sum_{z\in H(a,b)}\mathbf 1\{D_z(Q_\tau)\ge D_{z^{\mathrm{obs}}}(Q_\tau)\}\).

definitions.name: Assignment crossings
definitions.construction: For \(z\in H(a,b)\setminus\{z^{\mathrm{obs}}\}\), set \(t_z=\{D_{z^{\mathrm{obs}}}(Y^{\mathrm{obs}})-D_z(Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\}/\{1-D_z(X^{\mathrm{obs}})\}\), and order these values with multiplicity as \(t_{(1)}\le\cdots\le t_{(h(a,b)-1)}\).

definitions.name: Inverted confidence set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}=\{\tau\in\mathbb R:p_\tau>\alpha\}\) and \(k_\alpha=\lfloor\alpha h(a,b)\rfloor\).

definitions.name: Certified finite fallback
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Enum}(n_B,n_S,R)\) enumerates every positive paired composition of totals \((2n_B,2n_S)\) up to common permutations, computes \([x^{n_B}y^{n_S}]\prod_\ell(1+x^{a_\ell}y^{b_\ell})\) by the recurrence \(d_{\ell+1}(i,j)=d_\ell(i,j)+d_\ell(i-a_{\ell+1},j-b_{\ell+1})\), and returns every feasible maximizer and its objective.

definitions.name: Paired-residual purification handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Purify}_R\) denotes the program that starts from a residual entry in \(\mathcal C_R\), applies a Singhal-style pure-profile decomposition jointly to the two subset-sum profiles toward \(\mathcal U_R\), preserves a common target fiber, and tracks the change in \(F\) and \(h\) through every elementary compression.

statements.statement: For every \(c\in\mathcal C_R\), the induced profile \((m+2,a_c,b_c)\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{n_B,n_S}(R)\), satisfies \(h(a_c,b_c)=2N_c\), and has \(F(a_c,b_c)=f_c(n_B,n_S)\).
statements.justification: Exact catalog support rules out hidden assignments that would invalidate both the support floor and the phase formula.
statements.gap: Neither Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis's equal blocks nor Singhal's one-profile concentration theorem provides a bivariate residual-fiber identity.
statements.consumer: The result lets an experimenter evaluate every large-margin candidate using a finite table depending only on \(R\).

statements.statement: Orient the sides so \(n_B\le n_S\). Every maximizer \((L,a,b)\in\mathcal A_{n_B,n_S}(R)\) has, after a common block permutation, two large paired blocks and residual totals \(A\le2\lceil R/2\rceil-1\le R\) and \(D<2A\le2R\); its residual tuple belongs to \(\mathcal C_R\). The analogous statement holds after swapping the sides when \(n_S<n_B\).
statements.justification: The ratio-uniform residual bound is the structural step that converts an unbounded design search into a finite frontier.
statements.gap: The closest block construction fixes equal square blocks, and the general biclique literature has no two-margin concentration or equality classification.
statements.consumer: The bound makes optimal exact-test conditioning computable even when buyer and seller populations have extreme aspect ratios.

statements.statement: For every \(R\ge4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), \(\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)=\max_{c\in\mathcal C_R}f_c(n_B,n_S)\). Every maximizing profile is one of the catalog argmax profiles, modulo a common block permutation and simultaneous complementation \((p,q)\mapsto(A-p,D-q)\); conversely every catalog argmax is an optimizer. Hence the quadrant is partitioned by the rational affine inequalities \((D_d-D_c)n_B+(A_d-A_c)n_S\ge K_d-K_c\) into exact phase cells retaining all equality cases.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: an exact all-resolution value and a complete equality classification over unequal margins.
statements.gap: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis provide a chosen \(k\)-block family and a heuristic trade-off, while Puelz et al. provide approximate biclique search rather than an explicit structured optimum.
statements.consumer: A platform can choose the largest focal rectangle attaining a prespecified exact-test resolution before inspecting outcomes.

statements.statement: When \(n_B=n_S\), \(\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)\ge\Phi_{n_B}^{\mathrm{eq}}(R)\). The containment is strict: at \(n_B=n_S=16\) and \(R=4\), \(\Phi_{16,16}(4)=452>256=\Phi_{16}^{\mathrm{eq}}(4)\).
statements.justification: A concrete strict delta distinguishes the catalog from a notational enlargement of the published equal-block family.
statements.gap: The published equal-square calculation does not optimize over unequal block sizes even on a square population.
statements.consumer: Researchers using the published \(k\)-block rule obtain a certified focal-size improvement without changing the randomization design.

statements.statement: For every positive \((n_B,n_S,R)\), \(\mathsf{Enum}(n_B,n_S,R)\) terminates, returns \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\) exactly when \(\mathcal A_{n_B,n_S}(R)=\varnothing\), and otherwise returns \(\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(R)\) and every maximizing paired multiset. Its recurrence table and terminal objective list form a checkable finite certificate.
statements.justification: The finite fallback closes every margin below the analytic threshold without claiming an unsupported complexity bound.
statements.gap: Generic biclique search is NP-hard and the closest exact-test papers do not give a complete certificate for the structured small-margin problem.
statements.consumer: Small marketplace pilots receive an auditable exact design choice rather than an asymptotic or large-margin approximation.

statements.statement: Fix any admissible profile selected without assignments or outcomes. Under \(\mathsf{Sample}_{ZP}\), every \(Z\in\Omega\) is incident to exactly \(\nu(a,b)\) compatible ordered paired partitions. Conditional on the reported \(P\), the induced pattern \(z^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is uniform on \(H(a,b)\), equivalently \(Z\) is uniform over the full assignments compatible with \(P\). The sampler is equivariant under independent relabelings of \(B\) and \(S\).
statements.justification: Correct conditional sampling is required for the frontier to define an exact test rather than only a combinatorial optimum.
statements.gap: Basse et al. derive uniform exposure orbits from equivariance, but unequal rectangular auxiliary partitions require an explicit constant-fiber count.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies a rejection-free implementation of every catalogued event under unequal buyer and seller population sizes.

statements.statement: Under the sharp constant total-effect null, \(Q_{\tau,ij}=Y_{ij}(0,0)\) on \(U_P\), and for every \(0<\alpha<1\), \(\Pr\{p_\tau\le\alpha\mid P,Q_\tau\}\le\lfloor\alpha h(a,b)\rfloor/h(a,b)\le\alpha\). For the focal-dyad difference in means, \(1-D_z(X^{\mathrm{obs}})>0\) for every \(z\ne z^{\mathrm{obs}}\); if \(k_\alpha=0\), then \(\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}=\mathbb R\), while if \(k_\alpha\ge1\), then \(\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}=[t_{(k_\alpha)},\infty)\). Thus \(\Pr\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The result turns exact point-null validity into an effect-size confidence statement with the correct discrete endpoint.
statements.gap: Luo et al. give general inversion conditions and Liu et al. treat the zero total-effect null, but neither derives this null-adjusted dyadic crossing formula.
statements.consumer: The Platform O design can report an exact lower confidence bound for a constant dyad-level total effect under the stipulated exposure model.

statements.statement: For \(n_B,n_S\ge3\), \(\Phi_{n_B,n_S}(4)=2(n_B-1)(n_S-1)+2\), with unique paired multiset \(\{(n_B-1,n_S-1),(n_B-1,n_S-1),(1,1),(1,1)\}\) modulo block permutation.
statements.justification: The lowest nondegenerate resolution is a transparent sanity check on the catalog and its equality accounting.
statements.gap: This closed rectangular special case is not stated in the equal-block or general biclique papers.
statements.consumer: An experiment requiring four assignments obtains an immediate design rule without catalog enumeration.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathsf{Purify}_R\) be realized so that, for every \(c\in\mathcal C_R\), its output \(c'\in\mathcal U_R\) satisfies \(2N_{c'}\ge2N_c\) and \(f_{c'}(n_B,n_S)\ge f_c(n_B,n_S)\) simultaneously for all \(n_B,n_S\ge4R\), with equality conditions tracked in both directions?
statements.justification: A positive answer would collapse the finite affine envelope to a closed all-resolution formula and expose the true extremal mechanism.
statements.gap: Singhal's pure-profile reduction does not preserve a chosen common bivariate fiber, and the current catalog theorem bounds residual size without purifying residual shape.
statements.consumer: Designers could compute the optimal rectangle in closed form for arbitrary \(R\), eliminating catalog enumeration in large experiments.

sampling_model.design: Independent uniform complete randomization on \(B\) and \(S\), with exactly \(n_B\) treated buyers and \(n_S\) treated sellers.
sampling_model.units: The finite populations \(B\) and \(S\) and all dyad potential outcomes are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: A dyad has exposure \((z_i^B,z_j^S)\in\{0,1\}^2\); the tested contrast compares \((1,1)\) with \((0,0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No superpopulation overlap condition is used; positivity is the finite support condition \(h(a,b)\ge R\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The procedure enumerates or exactly samples the conditional randomization law.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 establishes that Procedure 3.2 is valid for any block size \(k\).
The randomization test described in Procedure 1 is valid conditionally at any level.
If \(T\) is imputable, the randomization test is valid at any level \(\alpha\).
Then, \(W\) is uniformly distributed conditional on the event \(\{W\in\mathcal B\}\).
If \(T\) is effect increasing, then \(p^{L+}(D^{\mathrm{obs}},\theta)\) is non-decreasing in \(\theta\).
The concentration probability is maximized when all the \(a_i\) are \(\pm1\).

tldr: Independent half-randomization on two market sides creates many exact conditional tests, but no rule currently identifies the covering rectangle that retains the most dyads at a required randomization resolution. The central result reduces this margin-sized combinatorial optimization to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\), proves every optimizer is captured uniformly over aspect ratios, and gives the exact affine phase envelope and all equality cases. A constant-incidence sampler implements every optimal event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield an exact one-sided confidence ray for a sharp constant total effect.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice heuristically; general biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but not an extremal classification of covering product slices.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles, a structure narrow enough for exact extremal analysis but rich enough to improve materially on equal blocks.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument first bounds the residual on the smaller side and then copies that residual to the larger side without losing support, producing a finite catalog, an exact phase formula, an implementable conditional law, and exact inversion.

related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off; the present frontier strictly enlarges that design class and certifies its optimum. Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, which informs the objective but does not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) supply the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) supply the orbit-equivariance template, while the unequal rectangular sampler requires a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) supply discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here only after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are proved. Singhal (2019) supplies the bilinear subset-sum profile and purification viewpoint, but not a coupled fixed-cardinality common-fiber extremum. Ye et al. (2023) provide the concrete unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
technical_internal_limitation: The conditioning event must be selected without outcomes. Raw focal outcomes are not imputable under a nonzero sharp constant effect; the null-adjusted array \(Q_\tau\) is essential. Complement symmetry also implies that an ordinary nonrandomized absolute-score test has minimum \(p\)-value at least \(2/h(a,b)\), so support \(20\) cannot support an ordinary two-sided test at level \(0.05\).
honest_scope: The finite-catalog theorem, affine envelope, sampler, and one-sided sharp-null inversion are to be proved. Universal unit residuals remain an explicit open-ended question. The proposal makes no claim about weak-null validity, power optimality, confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, a minimal \(4R\) threshold, or the validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O. For the standard check \(R=4\), the frontier reduces to the stated four-block formula and unique paired multiset.

seed_details.question: Does every retention-maximizing covering rectangle with at least \(R\) common half-sum assignments admit a residual representation whose two residual totals are bounded only by \(R\), uniformly over rectangular aspect ratios?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the equal-square block calculation after Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis's Theorem 3.2 by a two-margin concentration argument; the first new step is a support-preserving copy of the smaller-side residual profile onto the larger side.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for rectangular common-half-sum optimization, paired subset-sum profiles, and two-sided conditional-randomization rectangles found biclique heuristics and equal-block constructions but no exact coupled frontier.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that the result is immediate from the \(k\)-block calculation in Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis because only the number of blocks matters.
seed_details.rebuttal: Unequal paired block sizes create a coupled bivariate coefficient problem; their calculation neither bounds both residual margins nor classifies equality cases across arbitrary aspect ratios.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Singhal purifies each one-dimensional subset-sum profile separately and then uses bilinearity; here the first altered step must preserve one common two-dimensional fiber while improving a constrained bilinear retention score.

seed_details.rebuttal: That theorem maximizes one point mass without two covering constraints or a paired retention objective; even Singhal's pure objects do not preserve a specified common bivariate fiber.

seed_details.question: For three independently half-randomized populations, can a bounded-residual catalog optimize the tensor retention score \(\sum_\ell a_\ell b_\ell d_\ell\) at a common support floor?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The bilinear rearrangement and two-stage concentration fail when the objective becomes trilinear, before any residual-copy comparison can be applied.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for tensor common-half-sum randomization frontiers and three-sided marketplace conditional tests found no matching target--method pair.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical objection is that this is a speculative dimensional lift without an economic design in view.
seed_details.rebuttal: The trilinear obstruction is genuine, but the absence of a verified consumer and a viable concentration lemma makes the seed premature.

literature_map.settled: Finite-sample validity is settled once imputability and the conditional assignment law are correct; equal \(k\)-block total-effect events and general biclique constructions are also settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No inspected theorem maximizes \(\sum_\ell a_\ell b_\ell\) over all covering paired rectangles at a common-half-sum support floor or classifies every optimizer.
literature_map.method_adapted: The proof adapts Singhal's bilinear-profile viewpoint and equality tracking, but replaces independent purification by a support-preserving residual-copy competitor; it adapts Puelz et al.'s focal-units-by-assignments trade-off only as motivation.

literature_map.settled: Singhal proves reduction to \(\{-1,1\}\) coefficients for a one-dimensional concentration probability, while the finite catalog below settles bounded residual size without settling residual shape.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No inspected paper gives a support-preserving purification of a prescribed bivariate fixed-cardinality fiber under the retention objective.
literature_map.method_adapted: The handle imports pure-profile decomposition and equality propagation, with common-fiber preservation imposed at the first decomposition step.

literature_map.settled: Independent two-sided complete randomization allows arbitrary fixed treated counts, and marketplace work shows allocation fractions matter for bias and variance.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: No inspected theorem couples the two asymmetric fixed-cardinality subset-sum profiles into an exact rectangular support--retention frontier.
literature_map.method_adapted: Singhal's asymmetric concentration analysis supplies a plausible replacement for complement symmetry, but a two-profile extremal theorem is not yet available.
